School Setup Process

1. Configure school identity

Admin updates school profile in School Setup.

2. Configure academic years

Admin creates and activates sessions in Academic Years.

3. Define academic groups

Admin maintains grouping in Academic Groups.

Academic Configuration Process

1. Structural configuration

Configure classes/sections, shifts, and classrooms from the School Management menu.

2. Curriculum configuration

Configure subjects and class-subject mappings to establish teaching scope.

3. Teacher allocation

Create teachers, assign subject-teacher links, and monitor workload.

4. Timetable publication

Create section timetable and resolve scheduling/resource conflicts.

Admission & Student Lifecycle Process

1. Admission setup

Admin/Admission Officer configures rules, document types, and identity rules.

2. Application intake

Applicants submit data using online application.

3. Verification and decision

Application team reviews and approves/rejects in Student Applications.

4. Onboarding

Approved applicants become students and are visible in Students.

5. Lifecycle management

Admin manages updates, promotions, section changes, inactivity, transfers, guardian linkage, and exports.

Application Process (Detailed Operational Flow)

Stage Primary Actor System Action Result
Public intake open Admin Publishes admission info and enables public intake window. Candidates can apply from public portal.
Application submission Applicant / Parent Submits candidate profile and required data from public apply form. Unique application tracking number is generated.
Status tracking Applicant / Parent Checks status with tracking number + DOB. Candidate gets secure public progress visibility.
Admission payment Applicant / Parent Uses make-payment page to pay via bKash/online bank or submit bank transfer. Payment status moves to paid or pending verification.
Payment governance Admin / Admission Officer Reviews/adjusts payment, updates references, and controls final fee state. Payment state aligned for admission decision.
Application decision Admission Officer / Admin Verifies documents and performs accept/reject workflow. Accepted applications become eligible for admit card and enrollment.
Admit card / receipt generation Admin / Admission Officer Generates admit card and payment receipt artifacts for valid paid cases. Candidate receives admission-ready documents.
Enrollment and section assignment Admin Converts approved applicant to student and assigns class/section. Student record is onboarded into lifecycle operations.
Student onboarding invite System + Admin Sends onboarding invite through student/guardian email for portal access. Candidate can onboard and use system services.
Post-login role pages Student / Guardian After invite acceptance and login, user lands on role-appropriate pages (student self pages or guardian linked-student pages). Role-based consumption starts immediately.

Attendance Business Process

1. Policy configuration

Admin configures threshold, late rules, lock window, holidays, and weekends.

2. Daily marking

Teacher marks attendance by class/section/subject/date (Present/Absent/Late/Leave).

3. Notification processing

System creates absence notifications and logs dispatch status.

4. Review and reporting

Admin and staff monitor reports; student/guardian can access personal or linked views.

5. Edit governance

Teachers submit edit requests with reason; admin approves or rejects with full change trace.

Exam Business Process

1. Schedule management

Teacher/admin creates schedule (class, section, subject, term, type, date/time).

2. Clash/approval stage

Admin reviews conflict indicators, approves/rejects, and controls readiness.

3. Publish timetable

Published schedule becomes visible in student/guardian exam views.

4. Marks entry

Teacher enters marks with max validation and draft/final submission logic.

5. Result publication

Admin publishes results by class/term and the system locks post-publish edit path.

6. Post-publication workflows

Correction requests, exam paper upload, and analytics monitoring continue with permission control.

Fees & Payments Business Process

1. Fee structure setup

Admin defines fee heads, terms, templates, pricing rules, and schedules under Fee Settings.

2. Assignment

Admin assigns fee templates/schedules to students (manual, auto, or auto-on-enrollment) via the Fees Workspace assignments.

3. Invoice generation

Admin generates invoices in bulk (by class/cohort) or individually; invoices are delivered to guardians and tracked for delivery status.

4. Collection

Guardian pays online (bKash/online bank via Payment Management, never a direct gateway call) or submits a bank-transfer proof for admin verification; admin can also record counter collection.

5. Adjustment and governance

Admin issues refunds/credit-notes (never mutating a settled record directly) and can close or override a billing period with an audit trail.

6. Reporting

Admin reviews outstanding, collection-summary, defaulters, discounts, and refunds-adjustments reports, plus the fee audit log.

Fees & Payments Business Process (Detailed Operational Flow)

Stage Primary Actor System Action Result
Fee structure setup Admin Defines fee heads, terms, templates, pricing rules, and schedules. Reusable fee structure ready for assignment.
Assignment Admin Assigns fee templates/schedules to students (manual, auto, or auto-on-enrollment). Students have an active fee obligation.
Invoice generation Admin Generates invoices in bulk or individually and tracks delivery to guardians. Guardians receive a payable invoice.
Collection Guardian Pays online (bKash/online bank), submits a bank-transfer proof, or pays at the counter. Payment recorded as paid or pending verification.
Adjustment and governance Admin Issues refunds/credit-notes or closes/overrides a billing period. Fee ledger stays accurate with a full audit trail.
Reporting Admin Reviews outstanding, collection-summary, defaulters, discounts, and refunds-adjustments reports. Leadership has an accurate fee-collection picture.

Public Website Business Process

1. Identity setup

Admin configures school identity/branding (shared prerequisite with School Setup).

2. Content authoring

Admin configures Public Page Settings sections (hero, navigation, feature cards, about, downloads, gallery, social, footer, legal pages) and publishing/SEO settings.

3. Notices and events

Admin authors public notices and events through their respective editor pages.

4. Public consumption

Anonymous visitors view the published organization page and admissions entry point.

Detailed Sequence Matrix

Module Step Actor Action Output
Setup 1 Admin Configure identity/session/groups Tenant academic baseline ready.
Academic Config 2 Admin Configure classes, subjects, teachers, timetable Operational academic map ready.
Admission 3 Admission Officer Process applications and decisions Approved candidate pool.
Student Lifecycle 4 Admin Onboard and manage students/guardians Active student records.
Attendance 5 Teacher Daily marking and corrections Accurate attendance history.
Exams 6 Teacher/Admin Schedule, marks, publish, corrections Timetable, results, and analytics.

Controls & Governance

  1. Use least-privilege role assignment from Roles.
  2. Attendance and exam modifications after lock/publish must follow correction workflow.
  3. Operational actions require active tenant context and membership validation.
  4. Approval/publish stages are control points and should remain limited to admin-level roles.

/app/finance/system-detail:
Finance System Detail

Finance Business Flow and System Detail

Use this page to understand how the finance application is structured across master data, subledgers, banking, reconciliation, reporting, controls, and period-end operations.

AudienceFinance lead, implementation team, controller, auditor, project owner
Use this page forProcess alignment, implementation review, training, and system walkthrough

Operating model

Stage Business meaning Primary pages System result
Master setup Define accounts, periods, partners, banks, and global finance settings. Accounts, Periods, Partners, Banking, Integrations Finance foundation is ready for transaction processing.
Operational posting Create journals, invoices, bills, receipts, and payments. Journals, Receivables, Payables Subledgers and GL stay synchronized through posting journals.
Cash and reconciliation Monitor bank balances and reconcile bank statements against books. Banking, Reconciliation Cash records are validated against external bank evidence.
Analysis and planning Review budgets, cost centers, assets, and financial statements. Budgets, Cost Centers, Fixed Assets, Reports Management obtains financial visibility and control.
Close and compliance Prepare tax returns, run FX revaluation, review aging and statements, and close periods. Reports, Periods Books move toward period-end readiness with audit support.

Foundation and controls

  1. The chart of accounts is the system backbone; every finance transaction eventually posts into it.
  2. Accounting periods control when postings are allowed and form the basic close discipline.
  3. Bank accounts link treasury operations to specific cash or bank GL accounts.
  4. Integration settings centralize base currency, FX accounts, tax codes, exchange rates, and inter-module mappings.
  5. Business partners standardize customer and supplier identity across subledgers.

Transaction flows

Flow Business sequence System effect
Manual journal Create draft, optionally approve, post, reverse if necessary. Direct GL movement with full audit trail.
Sales invoice Create draft invoice, review, post, collect receipt, monitor balance. AR is debited, revenue and tax are credited, later cleared by receipt.
Purchase bill Create draft bill, review, post, make payment, monitor balance. Expense and input tax are debited, AP is credited, later cleared by payment.
Receipt / payment Allocate receipt or payment to open documents. Cash moves with AR or AP relief and FX settlement handling where applicable.
Recurring journal Define template, activate, run on schedule or manually. Repeatable postings are standardized and controlled.

Receivables and payables lifecycle

Subledger Lifecycle steps Key control points
Accounts Receivable Invoice draft -> approval/review -> post -> overdue monitoring -> receipt allocation -> partner statement Draft editability only before posting, approval status control, cancellation through reversal, overdue alerting
Accounts Payable Bill draft -> approval/review -> post -> due monitoring -> payment allocation -> supplier statement Draft-only editing, payment cannot exceed open balance, cancellation with reversals, overdue monitoring

Banking and reconciliation

Area How it works
Bank account register Each bank account provides a transaction register view derived from posted journal lines against its linked GL account.
Statement import Users import statement periods with opening balance, closing balance, and detailed statement lines.
Auto-match The system attempts to match statement lines against posted journal activity within the statement period.
Manual resolution Users can exclude unmatched lines and finalize once all items are resolved.
Finalization Reconciliation status moves from pending to reconciled and stores user/time metadata for audit review.

Period-end, tax, FX, and reporting

Function How it fits into close Primary page
Financial statements Review trial balance, general ledger, profit and loss, and balance sheet before close. Reports
Aging and partner statements Review AR/AP exposure, collect confirmations, and follow up on overdue balances. Reports
Cash flow and cashbook Review liquidity movements and reconcile treasury activity. Reports
Budget vs actual Compare current spending or income against approved budgets. Reports
Tax return periods Create, prepare, file, and mark tax obligations paid using tax-liability data. Reports
FX revaluation Revalue open foreign-currency receivables, payables, and bank balances using exchange rates and FX gain/loss accounts. Reports
Period close Close accounting periods once transactions and controls are complete. Periods

Governance and audit

  1. Maker-checker controls are supported through draft, approval, post, and reversal patterns.
  2. Finance activity logs capture key operational actions across journals, invoices, bills, receipts, payments, budgets, assets, and compliance actions.
  3. Dashboard KPIs highlight operational risk quickly through overdue documents, open periods, draft activity, and cash visibility.
  4. PDF outputs for invoices, bills, receipts, payments, and partner statements provide document evidence for external or internal review.
  5. Bank reconciliation and period-end functions provide additional control checkpoints before close.
